newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa sells Telkom stake for $1.26 bln.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa sells Telkom stake for $1.26 bln.

text.p: South Africa clinched Sub-Saharan Africa's big privatisation deal Wednesday, selling a 30 percent stake in state utility Telkom to a U.S.-Malaysian consortium for $1.261 billion.
SBC Communications Inc., the San Antonio, Texas-based parent of Southwestern Bell, will pay 60 percent of the bill and Telekom Malaysia Bhd will pay 40 percent.
The deal, the first major sell-off of state assets in South Africa and the largest direct investment in the country to date, values Telkom at $4.2 billion.
Of the proceeds, $1 billion will be injected back into Telkom to help fund its infrastructure expansion programme and the balance will go to the state to cut government debt.

Posts, Telecommunications and Broadcasting Minister Jay Naidoo said the partial privatisation would provide badly-needed capital, expertise and technology to enable Telkom to overcome the legacy of the apartheid era.
Millions of South Africans, mainly blacks, have no access to a telephone while affluent, white suburbs enjoy first world standards of service.
"The restructuring of Telkom will provide universal access to telephony services and an information backbone for macroeconomic development," Naidoo said.
"Telkom will at the same time be transformed into a world-class operator."

Telkom and its strategic equity partners -- who will enjoy a five-year exclusivity period in fixed line telephone service -- have committed themselves to one of the fastest roll-out programmes in the world, promising to deliver 2.8 million new lines including 120,000 payphones over the next five years.
